h: A river, a queen and a few more surprises
p: One of the nicest things about Poole's Cavern is the water running through it. The River Wye rises close by and flows through the cave, and the sound of it adds to the atmosphere as you walk along. Look out too for the Mary Queen of Scots Pillar, a column of rock named after the famous queen, who is said to have visited during her time in Buxton.

The tours are a manageable length for families, long enough to feel like an adventure without testing younger children's patience. The guides are good at keeping things lively, so expect plenty of jokes alongside the history and geology. If you prefer the self-guided route, take your time and read the displays as you go.

Tips for your visit: bring a warm jumper and decent shoes, and arrive with time to spare so you can explore the visitor centre before your tour. If you're visiting on a busy weekend or in the school holidays, booking ahead is a wise move.

For thrill-seekers, there's a Go Ape treetop adventure in the woods of Buxton Country Park nearby, so older kids and adventurous adults can swap the underground for a high-ropes course. It's booked separately, but it makes a brilliant double act with the cave.

Back in town, the Buxton Opera House, the restored Crescent and the free-flowing spa water at St Ann's Well are all worth a look. Buxton is a lovely base for exploring the Peak District, with Chatsworth and Bakewell within a short drive.
